subject: President Volodymyr Zelensky, appearing to tell Ukrainian troops to surrender
claim: A video of Zelensky at a podium telling soldiers to lay down their arms appeared briefly on the hacked Ukraine 24 website, and the channel's TV ticker carried a written surrender message. Ukraine 24 and Zelensky said it was fake.
finding: Observers pointed to an out-of-proportion head, a voice that didn't match and the wrong accent. Ukrainian officials had warned weeks earlier that a fake surrender video might appear.
outcome: Zelensky quickly posted his own video rebutting it, and Meta removed the fake. In NPR's reporting, Sam Gregory of the human-rights group WITNESS suggested that Ukraine's advance warnings and Zelensky's quick reply helped limit its reach in the West. It still circulated elsewhere.
